newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Monday as the cabinet deliberated additional 1997 budget cuts, dealers said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor held a television appeal on Sunday for support for the cuts.

Netanyahu said on Monday that the Israeli cabinet was being asked to consider an additional budget cut of 1.2 billion shekels on top of the 4.9 billion shekels of cutbacks included in the original 1997 budget of 190.8 billion shekels.

"The session opened with a sharp decline of the shekel in the wake of the television interview. But when the dollar reached 3.29 shekels investors started selling dollars," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.

"The market is very nervous and trading was volatile. Investors are waiting for the budget's approval," he said, adding: "The market believes that eventually the shekel will decline against the dollar."
Later officials announced that the cabinet had approved the budget.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2820 shekels against 3.2730 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6617 shekels against 3.6599 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8971 shekels per 100 yen against 2.9176 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1142 shekels against 2.1240 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2800 shekels.
